observations: Photo 0: a small, low resolution photo of a used automatic car transmission seen from the bellhousing side, with a blue torque converter fitted.
Photo 0: the aluminium casing shows grime and surface oxidation; it sits among several other used gearboxes, as at a used parts dealer.
Photo 0: an axle output seal and the transaxle housing are visible on the left; it looks like a front wheel drive transaxle.
Photo 0: no brand, model code, ID tag or electrical connector is readable; the only text is a faint dealer watermark ending 'SPARE PARTS'.
Photo 0: the side with the wiring connector, valve body and pan is not shown, so the pin count cannot be seen.

identity.kind: used automatic car gearbox (front wheel drive transaxle with torque converter)
read_from: photo 0 bellhousing and torque converter shape

claims.evidence: No Toyota marking or transmission model code is readable in photo 0.
The electrical connector is not visible in photo 0.
Fitment needs the transmission ID tag or casting code, not shown.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo of the casing.
Internal condition cannot be seen in a photo.
Photo 0 shows a grimy, oxidised used casing sitting in a pile of used gearboxes.
No photo of bolts, seals or pan; cannot be judged remotely.
No clip of it running in a car or on a test bench.
No receipt or warranty document is shown; a used import gearbox from a parts pile rarely carries one.

risks.risk: It is not a Camry gearbox or not the stated years, so it does not fit the buyer's car
risks.proof: A sharp close photo of the transmission ID tag or cast model code on the casing
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced as a Camry gearbox; fitment unknown

risks.risk: Connector is not the stated 22 pin type
risks.proof: A close photo of the main wiring connector on the casing

risks.risk: Slipping, harsh shifting or internal damage
risks.proof: A clip of the gearbox fitted in a car, driving through all gears with the dash visible
risks.if_unproven: as not working, core for rebuild

risks.risk: Burnt fluid or metal debris inside
risks.proof: A photo of the pan removed or the fluid on a white cloth

proof_requests: A sharp close photo of the transmission ID tag or casting code
A close photo of the wiring connector showing the pin count
A clear photo of the whole unit from the side and the pan
A clip of the gearbox working in a car
response.reason: A car gearbox is priced by the car it fits, and no brand, model code or ID tag is readable in the single small photo, so not even a worst case price can be anchored. The 'like new, works perfectly' line is contradicted by the grimy used casing and cannot raise any price.
